solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One has a job keeping King in retreating soldiers' line

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the king is held inside the other letters
retreating means going back, so the soldiers and the line are read backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a row is a line
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A soldier with a role guards the monarch as the troops fall back in formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' reverses the soldiers and the line together, giving WORER, before 'keeping' takes in K.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker is a person employed, someone who holds a job.

clue.text: Exhausts listener with first incomplete point

indicators.note: first says the abbreviation for with goes at the front, before the listener

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens

indicators.note: incomplete means the word is missing its final letter

parts.note: south is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone tires an audience by leaving their opening argument unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts W ahead of EAR; 'incomplete' cuts the H from SOUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear out is to tire or use up completely, the same as exhausting.

clue.text: Give a good review on company's first major repair

parts.note: re means on, concerning
CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word major

parts.note: to mend is to repair

explanation.surface: A critic praises a firm's first big renovation job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes M from 'major'.
explanation.definitionFit: To recommend something is to speak favourably of it, giving it a good review.

clue.text: Heard setter had studied

indicators.note: heard tells us the words are spoken, so we want something that sounds like them

parts.note: the setter is I, so the setter had is I'd

explanation.surface: A rumour says the puzzle setter had done some studying.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is I in crosswords; I'D sounds like EYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyed means looked at closely, examined, so studied in the sense of scrutinised.

clue.text: Talked incoherently and is flushed following injection

indicators.note: following says the being flushed comes after the injection

parts.note: a jab is an injection, especially in British usage
be is the base form of is
flushed in the face means red

explanation.surface: A patient babbles and turns pink after getting a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is flushed' is read as 'be red', the infinitive standing in for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jabbering is fast, garbled talk that is hard to follow.

clue.text: In fact, posh colleague's supporting show

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means sitting underneath, so the posh colleague goes below the show

parts.note: an act is a show or performance
U means upper-class, posh
an ally is a colleague or partner

explanation.surface: A smart workmate turns out to be backing a theatrical production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' in a down clue puts U + ALLY under ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Actually is an adverb meaning in reality, the same as in fact.

clue.text: Miss Bishop's going ahead with governors to show old classroom feature

indicators.note: going ahead says the bishop's letter comes in front of the next piece

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to miss something is to lack it
a board of governors runs a school

explanation.surface: A school mistress, a bishop and the governors all appear at an old school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a teacher, but it is the verb LACK; 'going ahead' puts B before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackboard is the dark writing surface once standard at the front of classrooms.

clue.text: Treatment for addiction uses a herb remedy

indicators.note: remedy as a verb means to put right, so the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rehab clinic relies on a herbal cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remedy' rearranges A HERB.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab, short for rehabilitation, is a programme helping addicts recover.

clue.text: Moved quickly and was brave enough to grab terrorist's foot

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so the extra letter is held inside

parts.note: dared means was brave enough

indicators.note: the foot of a word is its last letter in a down clue

explanation.surface: A hero rushed in and seized an attacker by the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' gives T, the end of 'terrorist's'; 'to grab' puts it inside DARED.
explanation.definitionFit: Darted means moved suddenly and fast, like a dart.

clue.text: Go up on street rising sharply

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to go is a slang term to pee

explanation.surface: Climb a road that climbs sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is the slang verb PEE, which 'up' turns to EEP; 'Go up' looks like the definition but 'rising sharply' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep slope climbs at a sharp angle.

clue.text: Old article has point about space in it

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
N is north, a compass point
C is circa, about

indicators.note: in means the space sits inside the letters of it

parts.note: an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: An old piece of writing makes a point about outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's space, half an em wide; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means very old, belonging to the distant past.

clue.text: Tutor sees child in a tree playing

indicators.note: in means the child is placed within the other letters
playing suggests letters moving about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A tutor watches a youngster playing up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges A TREE as TEAER; 'in' puts CH inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher is one who instructs pupils, as a tutor does.

clue.text: Wrestling with problem zip

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
zip means nothing, zero, shown as O

explanation.surface: A wrestler has trouble with a stuck zip.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese style of heavyweight wrestling.

clue.text: Scripture grade by pupil in Lincoln's outstanding

parts.note: RE is religious education, the British school subject
a mark is a grade

indicators.note: in places the pupil inside the president's name

parts.note: Abe was President Lincoln's first name
L is a learner driver, a pupil

explanation.surface: A Lincoln pupil scores a top grade in scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Religious Education is a British school subject; L is the learner plate on a British car; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable means worthy of notice, exceptional, as outstanding does.

clue.text: Life's changed around old haunts in part of London

indicators.note: around means the letters go round the old abbreviation
changed means the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: to dog is to follow persistently, to haunt

explanation.surface: A life transformed around old familiar hangouts in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns LIFES into ISLEF; 'around' puts O inside. The Isle of Dogs is a peninsula in East London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Dogs is a district of East London in a bend of the Thames.

clue.text: Use any compound tense

indicators.note: compound as a verb means mix together, so the letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: A grammar instruction: use any compound tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like grammar, but it is the adjective meaning anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneasy means anxious, nervous, as tense does.

clue.text: Boy by lake's given duck more crumbled bread

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, O

indicators.note: crumbled means broken into pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A lad at a lake feeds a duck extra crumbs of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbled' rearranges MORE into OMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a large British loaf with diagonal slashes on its crust.

clue.text: Supplies online joke intended to be read aloud

parts.note: E stands for electronic, online
a quip is a witty joke

indicators.note: read aloud says the spoken form gives the letters, not the spelling

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A web joke is meant to be read out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: MEANT is said like MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment means the gear or supplies needed for a task.

clue.text: Affected posers swallowing drugs with Italian coffee

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something inside, so the drugs go within
affected means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so drugs is Es

explanation.surface: Pretentious types slip drugs into their Italian coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' rearranges the posers as ESPRSO and 'swallowing' takes in the drugs; 'Affected' looks like an adjective describing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong coffee made by forcing steam through grounds, an Italian style.

clue.text: Papers have a look-up time-line on icon worship

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: lo means look
RY is railway, a line

explanation.surface: Newspapers check a timeline about the worship of icons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns A LO into OLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is the worship of idols or images, venerating icons.

clue.text: Nowadays poetry's antagonistic

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the present era
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Modern poetry is hostile.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means opposing or hostile, which is antagonistic.

clue.text: Dog's heading off after good run in field

indicators.note: after says the dog piece follows the good run

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a hound is a dog

explanation.surface: A dog runs well in a field once it sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the dog's first letter, and 'after' places what is left behind G R.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground is an area of land or a sports field.

clue.text: Cause very loud echoes around court

indicators.note: around shows the echoes sit about the very loud letters

parts.note: echo is E in the NATO alphabet, so echoes are two Es
FF is fortissimo, very loud in music

explanation.surface: Something very noisy rings round a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts the two Es around FF.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect something is to bring it about, to cause it.

clue.text: Pull off getting parking by chance

parts.note: P is the sign for parking
luck means chance

explanation.surface: Finding a parking space through sheer luck.
explanation.definitionFit: To pluck is to pull off feathers or fruit, removing them with a tug.

clue.text: Undersea eco-system examination in Florida results in big argument

indicators.note: in places the reef and the exam inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida
a reef is an undersea ecosystem
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A study of Florida's coral reef ends in a fierce row.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is a chaotic fight or dispute open to everyone.

clue.text: Throw out complex Pelham bit

indicators.note: bit means a piece of the words, so the answer is a run of letters lifted from them

explanation.surface: Discard the fiddly Pelham bit, a horse's mouthpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: A Pelham is a type of horse's bit, which makes 'bit' look like part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to drive out or eject, throw out.

clue.text: Dad invested in ring with large gemstone

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so dad goes inside the ring

parts.note: a ring is round, the letter O
pa is dad

explanation.surface: Dad puts money into a ring with a big gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' places PA inside O + L.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent precious stone.

clue.text: Scream seeing wolf briefly straying behind hotel

indicators.note: behind says the wolf piece follows the hotel letter

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: straying means wandering off course, so the letters are rearranged
briefly means the word is cut short at its end

explanation.surface: A shriek at seeing a wolf wander past a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the final F, 'straying' rearranges the remaining three letters, and 'behind' places them after H.
explanation.definitionFit: A howl is a long loud cry, a scream.

clue.text: Setter's contrary wiles have uses!

indicators.note: contrary means turned the other way, so the setter's word is reversed

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
ploys are tricks, wiles

explanation.surface: The setter admits a perverse cunning has its uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Employs means makes use of, uses.

clue.text: Most trendy carbon spectacles in case

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
OO looks like a pair of spectacles
lest means in case

explanation.surface: The hippest specs come in a carbon-fibre case.
explanation.definitionFit: Coolest is slang for most fashionable or trendy.

clue.text: Discuss work issues off duty in social after negotiations

indicators.note: after says the social follows the negotiations

parts.note: talks are negotiations
a hop is a dance, a social gathering

explanation.surface: After talks, the delegates relax at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk shop is to chat about one's job outside working hours.

clue.text: Girl's gutted with horrid zit taking last opportunity to be glamorous

indicators.note: gutted means the inside letters are removed, leaving the outside ones
horrid suggests something messed up, so the letters are rearranged
last picks the final letter of the word opportunity

explanation.surface: A distraught girl with a nasty spot seizes her final chance to look stunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves GL; 'horrid' rearranges ZIT to ITZ; 'last' gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitzy means showily glamorous, full of sparkle.
